syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

chapters.title: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe

topics.title: The French Revolution and the Idea of the Nation

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the measures French revolutionaries used to create a collective national identity.
Explain the administrative reforms of Napoleon, including the Civil Code of 1804.
Analyse why reactions to French rule in conquered territories turned from welcome to hostility.

topics.title: The Making of Nationalism: Aristocracy, Middle Class and Liberalism

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish the landed aristocracy from the new middle classes and their role in national unity.
Explain the political and economic ideas of nineteenth-century liberalism.
Explain how the zollverein and economic nationalism promoted German unity.

topics.title: A New Conservatism after 1815 and the Revolutionaries

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the beliefs of conservatives after the defeat of Napoleon.
Identify the aims and provisions of the Treaty of Vienna of 1815.
Describe the role of Giuseppe Mazzini and secret societies in the revolutionary movement.

topics.title: The Age of Revolutions and the Romantic Imagination

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the July Revolution of 1830 and the Greek war of independence.
Explain how Romanticism and folk culture helped shape national feeling.
Analyse how language served as a tool of national resistance in Poland.

topics.title: Hunger, Hardship and the 1848 Revolution of the Liberals

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the economic hardships that led to popular revolts in the 1830s and 1840s.
Evaluate the aims, course and outcome of the 1848 revolution of the liberals and the Frankfurt parliament.
Analyse the debate over political rights for women within the liberal movement.

topics.title: The Making of Germany and Italy and the Case of Britain

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the process of German unification under Prussian leadership.
Trace the stages and leaders of Italian unification.
Explain how the British nation-state was formed through a long-drawn-out process.

topics.title: Visualising the Nation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why nations were personified as female allegories such as Marianne and Germania.
Interpret the symbols used in allegorical images of the nation.

topics.title: Nationalism and Imperialism

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the Balkans became a source of nationalist tension after 1871.
Evaluate how nationalism changed in the late nineteenth century and its link with imperialism.

topics.title: The First World War and the idea of satyagraha

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the First World War created a new economic and political situation in India.
Explain the idea of satyagraha as active, non-violent resistance based on truth.
Identify Gandhiji's early satyagrahas at Champaran, Ahmedabad and Kheda and the groups they supported.

topics.title: The Rowlatt Act, Khilafat and the call for Non-Cooperation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Indians opposed the Rowlatt Act and how the Rowlatt satyagraha unfolded.
Describe the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and the repression that followed.
Explain why Gandhiji joined the Khilafat issue to Non-Cooperation and how the movement was planned in stages.

topics.title: Differing strands within the Non-Cooperation Movement

concepts.learning_objective: Describe middle-class participation and the economic boycott in the towns, and why it slowed down.
Explain how peasants in Awadh and tribals in the Gudem Hills interpreted swaraj in their own ways.
Explain what freedom meant to Assam plantation workers under the Inland Emigration Act.

topics.title: Towards Civil Disobedience and the Salt March

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the withdrawal of Non-Cooperation, the Swaraj Party's council politics and the impact of the depression.
Describe the protests against the Simon Commission and the Lahore Congress demand for Purna Swaraj.
Explain why the Salt March was an effective symbol and how Civil Disobedience differed from Non-Cooperation.

topics.title: How participants saw Civil Disobedience and its limits

concepts.learning_objective: Compare why rich peasants, poor peasants, business classes, workers and women joined Civil Disobedience.
Explain the dalit demand for separate electorates and the outcome of the Poona Pact.
Analyse why large sections of Muslims felt alienated from the Congress-led movement.

topics.title: The sense of collective belonging

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the image of Bharat Mata came to symbolise the nation.
Explain how folklore revival and nationalist flags helped create a feeling of nationalism.
Evaluate how nationalist histories built pride in the past and why they could exclude some communities.

chapters.title: The Making of a Global World

topics.title: The pre-modern world: silk routes and travelling foods

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how trade, travel and migration linked distant societies long before modern globalisation.
Explain the silk routes as an example of pre-modern trade and cultural exchange between Asia, Europe and Africa.
Explain how foods and crops travelled between continents and how new crops changed lives.

topics.title: Conquest, disease and trade in the sixteenth century

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how germs such as smallpox helped the European conquest of the Americas.
Explain how the sea routes to Asia and America and American silver 'shrank' the world from the sixteenth century.
Explain why the centre of world trade moved westwards towards Europe.

topics.title: The nineteenth century: a world economy takes shape and the role of technology

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the three flows of international economic exchange: trade, labour and capital.
Trace how the abolition of the Corn Laws led to a global agricultural economy, migration and capital flows.
Analyse how technology such as refrigerated ships changed the meat trade and diets in Europe.

topics.title: Late nineteenth-century colonialism and rinderpest in Africa

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how European powers partitioned Africa and how exploration served imperial projects.
Explain how colonisers recruited African labour and how rinderpest helped them subdue Africa.

topics.title: Indian labour, entrepreneurs and trade in the global system

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the nineteenth-century indentured labour migration from India and the cultures it created.
Identify the Indian bankers and traders who financed export agriculture and traded abroad.
Explain the change in India's exports and how Britain's trade surplus with India worked in the multilateral settlement system.

topics.title: The inter-war economy: war, recovery and mass production

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the economic effects of the First World War as the first modern industrial war.
Explain why post-war recovery was difficult for Britain and for agricultural economies.
Explain mass production, the assembly line and the consumer boom in the US in the 1920s.

topics.title: The Great Depression and India

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the causes of the Great Depression, including agricultural overproduction and the withdrawal of US loans.
Describe the effects of the Great Depression on the US economy and its banking system.
Analyse how the Great Depression affected Indian trade, peasants and urban India differently.

topics.title: Rebuilding a world economy: the post-war era and globalisation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the lessons of the inter-war years and the institutions and fixed exchange rates of the Bretton Woods system.
Explain why newly independent countries formed the G-77 and demanded a new international economic order.
Explain the end of the Bretton Woods system and the relocation of industry to low-wage Asian countries.

topics.title: Before the Industrial Revolution: proto-industrialisation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain proto-industrialisation as large-scale production for international markets before factories, organised by merchants.
Explain why merchants turned to the countryside and why peasant households worked for them.

topics.title: The coming up of the factory and the pace of industrial change

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the cotton mill brought production under one roof and the advantages this gave.
Evaluate evidence that industrialisation in Britain was gradual and that new technology spread slowly.

topics.title: Hand labour and steam power; life of the workers

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why many Victorian industrialists preferred hand labour to machines.
Describe the hardships of workers in industrial Britain and their hostility to new technology.

topics.title: The age of Indian textiles and what happened to weavers

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the pre-colonial network of Indian textile trade and its breakdown with the rise of European companies.
Explain how the East India Company controlled weavers through gomasthas and advances, and how weavers responded.

topics.title: Manchester comes to India

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how British cotton imports led to the decline of Indian textile exports and weaving.
Explain how the American Civil War and raw cotton exports affected Indian weavers.

topics.title: Factories come up: entrepreneurs and workers

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the early Indian industrialists and the sources of their capital.
Describe the role of European Managing Agencies in Indian industry before the First World War.
Explain where Indian mill workers came from and the role of the jobber in recruiting them.

topics.title: The peculiarities of industrial growth

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how yarn production, the swadeshi movement and the First World War shaped Indian industrial growth.
Recognise that small-scale production predominated over registered factories in colonial India.
Analyse why handloom weaving survived and expanded in the twentieth century.

topics.title: Market for goods: advertisements, labels and calendars

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse how labels, calendars and images were used to create markets for new products.
Explain how Indian manufacturers used advertisements to carry the nationalist message of swadeshi.

chapters.title: Print Culture and the Modern World

topics.title: The First Printed Books in East Asia

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how woodblock printing began and spread in China and how its uses widened.
Explain how print reached Japan and shaped its urban visual culture, including ukiyo prints.

topics.title: Print Comes to Europe and Gutenberg's Press

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how paper and woodblock printing reached Europe and why manuscripts could not meet demand.
Describe Gutenberg's printing press, its sources and its effect on book production.

topics.title: The Print Revolution and Its Impact

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how print created a new reading public and blurred oral and reading cultures.
Explain the role of print in Martin Luther's challenge and the Protestant Reformation.
Analyse why print was feared as a carrier of dissent and how the Church tried to control it.

topics.title: The Reading Mania and the French Revolution

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the rise of literacy and new forms of popular literature in eighteenth-century Europe.
Evaluate the arguments linking print culture with the Enlightenment and the French Revolution.

topics.title: The Nineteenth Century: New Readers and Innovations

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how children, women and workers became important readers and writers in the nineteenth century.
Describe nineteenth- and twentieth-century innovations in printing technology and publishing strategies.

topics.title: India and the World of Print and Religious Debates

concepts.learning_objective: Describe India's manuscript tradition and its limits before print.
Trace how the printing press came to India and how early newspapers developed.
Explain how print shaped religious reform and public debates in nineteenth-century India.

topics.title: New Forms of Publication: Women and the Poor

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the new literary and visual forms, such as novels and mass-produced prints, that print made possible.
Explain how print changed women's reading and writing and the anxieties this produced.
Analyse how print reached poor people and gave voice to protests against caste and class oppression.

topics.title: Print and Censorship in Colonial India

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the colonial state's control over the press changed before and after 1857.
Analyse the Vernacular Press Act and the link between press repression and nationalist protest.
